title: Felipe Assis and Carter Brown v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: Specification 1 was sustained; Specifications 2 and 3 were not sustained because the SJC was unable to judge them. The appeal was sustained, and Presbytery’s divestiture of both ministers was reversed.
first_summary: Two ministers appealed South Florida Presbytery’s decision to divest them of office without censure after their congregations left the PCA. The SJC sustained the appeal and reversed the divestitures because the ministers had not automatically become without call: Presbytery had never formally dissolved their calls, and they remained actively engaged and accepted in ministry. They were restored to good standing, while Presbytery was directed to dissolve the existing calls and pursue a constitutionally permissible course.
summary: Two ministers appealed Presbytery’s divestiture of their offices after their congregations left the PCA. The SJC reversed because their calls had never been formally dissolved, so they were not automatically without call, and BCO 34-10 did not apply while they remained actively engaged and accepted in ministry. The SJC could not judge their fairness and pretext claims from the record. It restored them to good standing and required Presbytery to dissolve the existing calls before pursuing lawful alternatives.

sources.supports: Case identity, appeal, issue judgments, adopted reasoning, reversal, restoration to good standing, required further action, and SJC adoption.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Cases 2025-12 and -13 are a combined appeal by Assis and Brown against South Florida Presbytery; the SJC approved the decision 19-2-0 (p. 1, lines 14–21; p. 9, lines 379–385).
evidence_notes.dispute: Presbytery divested both ministers without censure under BCO 13-2 and 34-10; they appealed that action (p. 4, lines 155–160; pp. 4–5, lines 182–194).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The calls had never been formally dissolved, and the ministers remained actively engaged and accepted in ministry, making BCO 13-2 and 34-10 inapplicable; the divestitures were reversed (pp. 5–8, lines 231–339; p. 8, lines 364–370).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC could not judge alleged unfair fact-finding or pretextual exclusion from the record; Presbytery must dissolve the calls and may then pursue lawful alternatives (p. 8, lines 341–370).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference.
